parsed.faithful: extinguishable barely by the debtor's retiring or cancelling them, the pursuer, before a proof of the tenor is admitted, must condescend on such a casus amissionis, or accident by which the writing was destroyed, as when it was lost when in the creditor's possession; otherwise bonds that have been cancelled by the debtor on payment, might be reared up as still subsisting against him; But in writings which require contrary deeds to extinguish their effect, as allegations, dispositions, charters, etc. it is sufficient to libel that they were left, even casu fortuito.
